clues: This city sits in the far north of Israel, in a hilly land called Galilee. It is the highest city in the whole country.
High ground gives this city warm summers and cold winters with snow at times. The height is why winter can turn white here.
Long ago, Crusaders built a large fort here in the year eleven sixty-eight. That fort made the small town start to grow in power.
Jewish people from all over Europe once made this city a heart of Kabbalah. That branch of faith is still taught and learned here today.
Judaism counts this city as one of its four most holy spots. Just three more towns in the world hold that same high rank.
